i've been a little bored with new games lately so i decided to revisit this game which i hadn't played since it's release.

i really liked this game. i thought it was an a great follow up to farcry 3 which was the first game in the series i played. i've read that some people felt it wasn't very ambitious in that it didn't really change the farcry formula much. while that may be true i think it improved every aspect of the game. it still looks great and i think it combined a lot of interesting game mechanics seamlessly and had a good story with strong characters.

i think my favorite part was clearing the bases. i liked how i could decide how i wanted to clear them- whether i went stealthy or guns blazing and how you could use environmental aspects like the caged animals or alarms to your advantage. i also liked the hunting to improve your supply carrying capacity. i didn't do much racing but the vehicles were varied and i used them occasionally, it was nice that they bothered to add so many different types for people who like that kind of thing. using the radio towers to clear the map was cool too. i'm not the biggest platform jumper fan but i thought the pay off was worth the effort and it kind of broke up the game play so all in all it was a positive.

i would highly recommend the game to anyone as it still plays well and looks great. good value in my opinion.

now to nit pick some things i didn't like so much, but weren't so bad as to prevent me from thinking the game was really fun.

the first thing that bothered me about the game was that before it was released one of the creators- i don't know if it was a writer or producer- came out as being critical of the gamergate movement. he went so far as to say that one of the characters was based on anita sarkessian and something to the extent that this element was going to make a lot of gamers unhappy. besides this just being an stupid thing to do with regards to your potential audience it really influenced some of the decisions i made in the game. specifically i was totally against amita and was on team sabal even before i found out what each one was about. to be truthful on reflection i didn't really like the way amita was portrayed so i probably wouldn't have been on her side anyway but i was definitely influenced by the nonsense this producer/writer was spouting and didn't appreciate his influence on my decisions. it was a shitty thing to do and totally unedcessary. it really took me out of the game in a way that made it less enjoyable for me.

i also wasn't a big fan of the 'y' events. these were the missions where you dealt with the two druggies and were very trippy and psychedelic. here's the thing- i'm not against drugs at all, i've used them, i think they are fine, and in my opinion people should be able to use them in a safe manner if they want to. i also like psychedelic music and visuals. it was more the way the missions were implemented- they didn't make sense to me from a story standpoint and they weren't very challenging. they were just kind of an excuse to do trippy visuals and have trippy music over and over and over. one long mission in that style instead of three or four relatively short ones would have been a better way to do it, but there were so many and they were so trivial that it seemed like an over indulgence or maybe even a cheap way to add content. i also have trouble believing ajay would have had anything to do with those guys after they slipped him a mickey in the first of the missions.

if i remember correctly farcry 3 had some kind of trippy missiond too and i really didn't like them much either so take this criticism with a grain of salt. maybe they were funnier than they seemed to me and i'm just a tight ass.

i also wasn't a big fan of the shangrila missions. i know there were optional, heck the 'y' missions were too but i liked the game so much it was hard to resist doing them to be honest. they were done ok but i just didn't find them interesting enough to want to slog through them. the tiger was kind of cool but i didn't like being limited to a bow even though i used it a lot during the regular game. i also didn't like the narration very much. it was cool to hear what i assume was tibetan being spoken but there was too much action going on for me to be able to read the subtitles so i pretty much missed the whole story during these missions and it might have made them more interesting.

so that's about it. i really, really liked this game and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for something to play. besides a few little niggles that might not bother you at all i think it was a very well done game.
